item.title: INDI alliance’s freebie politics exposed: DMK rolls out cash, laptops as ‘welfare’ ahead of 2026 Tamil Nadu polls after accusing BJP of ‘Vote Revdi’ in Bihar
item.description: Congress and DMK accused the BJP of engaging in corrupt practices over providing 10,000 to each woman in Bihar.

item.title: SC rules, ‘Reserved category candidates scoring above the general cut-off can’t be denied open seats’: Read what it means, and how it is not about ‘double benefit’
item.description: The Supreme Court ruled that reserved category candidates scoring above the General cut-off on merit can claim open seats, if they have not used any other caste-based relaxations. Dismissing Rajasthan HC recruitment appeals, it emphasised open categories belong to no caste, ensuring fairness under Articles 14 and 16

item.title: With Indus Water Treaty paused, India proceeds with multiple hydropower projects: Read how Modi govt is putting a stop to Pakistan taking unfair share of India’s rivers
item.description: Amidst the suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty, India is accelerating hydropower development in the upper Chenab basin to boost energy security, utilise water resources, and deprive Pakistan of the unfair reception of India’s waters.

item.title: Explained: PM-DeVINE and How it is transforming government school education in Assam
item.description: PM-DeVINE is upgrading Assam's government schools with smart classrooms and modern facilities, as highlighted by CM Himanta Biswa Sarma. The 1953 Palasbari school exemplifies the transformation, blending technology with traditional values to enhance learning and support state education reforms

item.title: Beyond outrage without strategy: Here is a 10-step roadmap that the Indian govt can follow to protect Hindus in Bangladesh
item.description: We are often told, “The Indian government is not doing enough to save Hindus in Bangladesh.”It is emotionally satisfying. But, what exactly should the government do? Spell out the roadmap. Because outrage without strategy may comfort the outraged, but it rarely protects the victim.

item.title: Before petroleum, there was bird poop: Read when Spain fought a war in South America, and US brought a law to claim islands. When empires went batsh*t crazy
item.description: To modern eyes, the idea that nations would go to war over bird poop seems laughable, but to 19th-century strategists, it was nothing short of essential.

item.title: Bharuch Jama Masjid dispute: Saints go on a hunger strike, call it a site of a pre-existing Jain temple; allege ASI norm violations
item.description: The Akhil Bharatiya Sant Samiti has accused the Bharuch Jama Masjid management of violating ASI rules, claiming the protected site is an ancient Jain temple and demanding an immediate survey and restoration of its original form.

item.title: Married to two, cheated a third and harassed another for 16 years: Bolta Hindustan ‘journalist’ Haseen Rahmani booked for blackmailing and raping a woman, read FIR details
item.description: In her complaint, the victim alleged that Bolta Hindustan journalist Haseen Rahmani trapped several girls, asking them to "please" politicians and close associates.

item.title: ‘Imaginary law-and-order bogey manufactured for political convenience’: Madras HC slams DMK’s political agenda, upholds lighting lamp at Thiruparankundram Hill
item.description: Calling the law-and-order threat an “imaginary ghost,” the Madras High Court upheld lamp lighting at Thiruparankundram Hill and exposed the DMK government’s agenda-driven obstruction.

item.title: Delhi Riots verdict explained: Why the SC rejected bail for Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam, seeing it as a planned conspiracy and not spontaneous violence
item.description: The Supreme Court ruled that the Delhi riots were a planned conspiracy, not spontaneous violence, drawing a firm line between alleged masterminds like Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam and peripheral actors while upholding strict UAPA bail norms.
